qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Deformation twin boundaries act as effective barriers to dislocation motion, reducing the dislocation mean free path (dynamic Hall-Petch effect); at RT this contributes only at the highest strains as very few twins form.

interaction_type.value: stress concentration at cell-block walls (planar slip)

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Type II and III grains form cell block walls with planar-slip characteristics that create the stress concentration required for twinning nucleation/growth, whereas type I grains form uniform dislocation cells that disperse macroscopic shear stress.

slip_behavior.value: At RT the early stage of deformation favours dislocation slip over twinning (the average {111}<110>_γ Schmid factor reaches its maximum near 3 % tensile strain, while the average {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor decreases at that strain). Planar slip dominates, with single glide traces in type II grains, double glide traces in type III grains and few slip traces in type I grains; type I grains form dislocation cells while type II and III grains form cell blocks.

phase_evolution.value: No phase transformation occurs during RT tensile deformation; the austenite (γ) fraction stays essentially constant (~97 %) and the ~3 vol.% BCC α ferrite is stable, even after large tensile strain.

interface_notes.value: Deformation twinning at RT is first observed after ~28 % tensile strain and remains of very low fraction up to 38 %; twinning occurs preferentially in type II and type III grains oriented away from <100>//TA.

Instrumented Charpy impact at RT: crack initiation energy Wm = 79.28 J and crack propagation energy Wp = 251.33 J (Fig. 2c); total impact energy at RT is governed by crack propagation energy.

True stress of the RT tensile specimen (Table 3): 339 MPa at 3.0 % engineering strain (3.0 % true strain), 483 MPa at 10.0 % (9.5 % true), 635 MPa at 20.0 % (18.2 % true), 723 MPa at 28.0 % (24.7 % true) and 800 MPa at 38.0 % (32.2 % true); not measured at 55 %.
Lattice friction stress of the austenite at RT is 143 MPa (calculated by Eq. 16 from the RT yield strength minus grain-boundary strengthening).

Experimental critical twinning stress at RT is about 723 MPa (Table 5), far smaller than the model estimates of 939 MPa (M = 2.2), 1153 MPa (M = 2.7), 1306 MPa (M = 3.06) and 1096 MPa (Hall-Petch-type relation).
At RT, deformation twinning is first observed after about 28 % tensile strain (a small fraction along cell-block walls), confirming that RT twinning occurs only just before necking.
Hardness is not reported for the RT tensile specimen (no hardness testing was performed).
